consensus_summary: Righteousness primarily denotes right standing before God (especially forensic/imputed righteousness of Christ credited by faith, not works) together with conformity to God’s moral character; ethical conduct, infused transformation, covenant faithfulness, and social justice appear as common or minority alternatives.
book_summary: Righteousness is the doing of God’s commandments—the law kept and worn as the garment of righteous acts—not a vague goodness nor a verdict only received.
rationale: The consensus responses uniformly place imputed/forensic right standing by faith at the center of the primary meaning and treat active obedience as a secondary ethical sense; the book inverts this hierarchy, defines righteousness as the kept law itself, and explicitly rejects a mere received verdict, thereby displacing the dominant common interpretation.
strongest_objection: Ethical/behavioral righteousness and the garment of righteous deeds are already catalogued as common alternatives within the consensus, so the book’s emphasis could be read as a sharpening of an existing strand rather than a contradiction.
